en: to deteriorate; to degenerate; to spoil

examples.en: In summer, milk goes bad easily.

examples.ko: 냉장고에 넣지 않으면 음식이 변질할 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you do not refrigerate it, the food can go bad.
The medicine has degraded, so you must not take it.

examples.ko: 원래 목적이 변질한 것 같아서 아쉬워요.
examples.en: It seems the original purpose has been corrupted, which is a pity.

examples.ko: 오래 두면 맛이 변질하고 색도 바뀌어요.
examples.en: If you leave it for long, the taste changes for the worse and the color changes too.
I will try so that my first intention does not get spoiled.

explain: 음식이나 약처럼 시간이 지나 성질이 나쁘게 바뀔 때 써요. 음식에는 '상하다', '쉬다'를 일상에서 더 자주 말해요. 처음의 뜻이나 마음이 나쁜 쪽으로 바뀌었다는 비유로도 써요.

phrases.en: The milk went bad in a day.
phrases.nuance_ko: '변질하다'보다 '변질되다'를 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: '변질되다' is more common than '변질하다'.

phrases.en: Don't eat food that has gone bad.
phrases.nuance_ko: 상한 음식을 꾸며 줄 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe spoiled food.

phrases.example: 밀봉하면 음식의 변질을 막을 수 있어요.
phrases.en: Sealing it can prevent food from spoiling.
phrases.nuance_ko: 상하지 않게 보관하는 방법을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when talking about how to keep things from spoiling.

explain_en: Food or materials going bad or altering; also values changing. Use it when food or medicine changes for the worse over time. In daily life 상하다 or 쉬다 is more common for food. It also works figuratively for an original purpose or feeling that has turned bad.

t90.ax: In summer, milk goes bad easily.

examples.en: He is an ardent worshipper of this singer.
The hero's worshippers gathered in the square.

examples.ko: 저는 돈의 숭배자가 되고 싶지 않아요.
examples.en: I don't want to become a worshipper of money.

examples.ko: 그 감독은 숭배자도 많고 비판하는 사람도 많아요.
examples.en: That director has many admirers and many critics too.
He was always surrounded by his worshippers.
I was once a devoted admirer of my teacher too.

explain: '팬'보다 훨씬 강하고 거의 종교처럼 떠받드는 느낌이에요. 가벼운 좋아함에는 '팬'을 쓰고, 숭배자는 무조건 따르는 사람을 조금 비꼬듯이 말할 때도 있어요.

phrases.en: That boy worships a soccer player.
phrases.nuance_ko: '숭배자'에서 나온 동사로, 누군가를 거의 우러러 받드는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The verb behind 숭배자; to look up to someone almost like a god.

phrases.en: I am a longtime fan of that singer.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가볍게 좋아하는 사람에게는 '숭배자' 대신 '팬'을 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: For someone who just likes something, use 팬 instead of 숭배자.

phrases.en: He is an ardent devotee of old movies.
phrases.nuance_ko: '열렬한'과 자주 같이 써서 아주 깊이 빠진 사람을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often paired with 열렬한 to describe someone deeply devoted.

explain_en: It is much stronger than '팬' (fan), with a feeling of near-religious devotion. For light liking, use '팬'; 숭배자 can also be said a little sarcastically about someone who follows blindly.

examples.en: I want to go on a space trip someday.
Space travel is still far too expensive.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 꿈은 우주여행을 하는 거였어요.
examples.en: My childhood dream was to travel into space.
If space travel becomes possible, will you go to the moon?

examples.ko: 아들은 우주여행 영화를 보고 우주비행사가 되고 싶어 해요.
examples.en: My son watched a space travel movie and now wants to be an astronaut.
I heard the training needed for space travel is really tough.

explain: '우주여행을 가다'와 '우주여행을 하다' 둘 다 자연스러워요. 아직은 영화, 뉴스, 미래 이야기에 자주 나오는 말이에요.

phrases.en: I want to travel in space someday.
phrases.nuance_ko: '가다'보다 우주에서 여행하는 경험 자체를 말할 때 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Focuses on the experience of traveling in space, rather than just going.

phrases.en: The main character in the movie sets off on a space trip.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이야기나 영화에서 여행을 시작하는 장면에 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often appears in stories and films for the start of a journey.
phrases.en_equiv: to set off on a space trip

phrases.en: I want to watch a space travel movie this weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: '우주여행' 뒤에 다른 명사를 붙여 주제를 나타내는 쓰임이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Putting a noun after 우주여행 names the topic, like a space travel movie.

explain_en: Both '우주여행을 가다' and '우주여행을 하다' sound natural. It still appears mostly in movies, news and talk about the future.

examples.en: The referee called a foul.

examples.ko: 그 선수는 파울이 너무 많아서 퇴장당했어요.
examples.en: That player had too many fouls and was sent off.

examples.ko: 농구는 파울을 다섯 번 하면 나가야 해요.
examples.en: In basketball, you have to leave after five fouls.

examples.ko: 야구에서 공이 선 밖으로 나가면 파울이에요.
examples.en: In baseball, if the ball goes outside the line, it's a foul.

examples.ko: 거친 파울 때문에 상대 선수가 다쳤어요.
examples.en: The opposing player got hurt because of a rough foul.

examples.ko: 파울 때문에 우리 팀이 자유투를 얻었어요.
examples.en: Thanks to a foul, our team got free throws.

explain: 축구, 농구, 야구에서 모두 '파울'이라고 하지만 뜻이 조금 달라요. 축구·농구는 규칙을 어긴 반칙이고, 야구는 공이 경기장 선 밖으로 나간 것이에요. 축구·농구의 파울은 '반칙'이라고도 해요.

phrases.en: The referee saw the foul and stopped the game.
phrases.nuance_ko: 축구·농구에서 '파울' 대신 쓸 수 있는 한국어 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A Korean word you can use instead of 파울 in soccer or basketball.

phrases.example: 그 선수는 한 경기에서 파울을 다섯 번 범했어요.
phrases.en: That player committed five fouls in one game.
phrases.nuance_ko: 규칙을 어기는 행동을 했다는 뜻이고, 중계나 기사에서 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means committing a rule violation; common in commentary and news.

phrases.example: 야구장에서 파울 볼이 우리 쪽으로 날아왔어요.
phrases.en: A foul ball flew toward us at the baseball park.
phrases.nuance_ko: 야구에서 선 밖으로 나간 공을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: In baseball, a ball hit outside the foul line.

explain_en: Korean uses 파울 in soccer, basketball and baseball, but the meaning shifts: in soccer and basketball it is a rule violation, while in baseball it means the ball landed outside the line. In soccer and basketball a 파울 is also called 반칙.

examples.en: A hacker broke into the company's server.
The news said hacker attacks have increased.
He handles computers like a hacker.
I change my password often to keep hackers out.

examples.ko: 보안 회사는 해커에게 시스템을 시험해 보게 했어요.
examples.en: The security firm had a hacker test its system.
A hacker and a security expert had a discussion together.

explain: 한국어 뉴스에서 '해커'는 보통 남의 컴퓨터에 몰래 들어가 나쁜 일을 하는 사람으로 들려요. 컴퓨터를 잘 다루는 사람은 '개발자'나 '프로그래머'라고 해요. 좋은 목적으로 보안을 점검하는 사람은 '화이트 해커'라고 불러요.

phrases.en: The website stopped because of a hacker attack.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스에서 보안 사고를 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used in news about security incidents.

phrases.en: A hacker hacked my account.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나쁜 일을 당했다는 뜻으로 '-당하다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: -당하다 shows that something bad happened to you.

phrases.example: 화이트 해커가 보안 문제를 찾아 줬어요.
phrases.en: A white hat hacker found the security problem.
phrases.nuance_ko: 좋은 목적으로 보안을 점검하는 해커예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A hacker who checks security for a good purpose.

explain_en: In Korean news '해커' usually sounds like someone who breaks into computers for bad purposes. Someone who is just good with computers is a '개발자' or '프로그래머'. A person who tests security for a good purpose is called a '화이트 해커'.

en: to be sensed; to be detected

examples.en: If smoke is detected, an alarm goes off.
A small earthquake was detected last night.

examples.ko: 센서에 사람의 움직임이 감지돼서 불이 켜졌어요.
examples.en: The sensor detected a person's movement, so the light turned on.

examples.ko: 이상한 소리가 감지되는 순간 기계가 멈췄어요.
examples.en: The moment a strange sound was detected, the machine stopped.
We are analyzing the signal that was detected.

examples.ko: 병원 검사에서 아무 문제도 감지되지 않았어요.
examples.en: No problems were detected in the hospital test.

explain: 기계, 센서, 검사가 눈에 안 띄는 신호나 변화를 알아챘다는 뜻이에요. 사람이 느끼는 건 '느끼다', 기계가 알아채는 건 '감지되다'를 써요. 뉴스에서는 지진, 연기, 소음, 이상 징후 이야기에 자주 나와요.

phrases.example: 문 앞에서 움직임이 감지되면 불이 켜져요.
phrases.en: The light turns on when movement is detected at the door.
phrases.nuance_ko: 센서가 알아챈다는 뜻으로 가장 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common phrase for a sensor picking something up.

phrases.en: No particular abnormality was detected in the test.
phrases.nuance_ko: 검사나 기계가 아무것도 알아채지 못했다고 부정할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Negative past form saying a test or machine detected nothing.

phrases.en: I could feel the building shake slightly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이 몸이나 마음으로 알아챌 때 쓰고, '감지되다'는 주로 기계가 알아챌 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a person senses something; 감지되다 is mostly for machines.

explain_en: A machine, sensor or test picks up a signal or change that isn't obvious. When a person feels it, use 느끼다, and when equipment catches it, use 감지되다. In news it often appears with earthquakes, smoke, noise and warning signs.

en: to be fixed; to become permanent; to become entrenched

examples.ko: 어릴 때 생긴 버릇이 어른이 되면 고착돼요.
examples.en: A habit formed in childhood becomes fixed once you are an adult.

examples.ko: 잘못된 자세가 고착되기 전에 고쳐야 해요.
examples.en: You should fix a bad posture before it becomes set.
In that region, poverty has become entrenched.
Once an image becomes fixed, it is hard to change.

examples.ko: 성별에 대한 편견이 고착되어 있다는 지적이 나왔어요.
examples.en: People pointed out that prejudice about gender has become entrenched.

examples.ko: 시험 방식 때문에 암기식 공부가 고착됐어요.
examples.en: Because of the exam format, studying by memorization has become the norm.

explain: '굳어지다'와 비슷하지만 더 딱딱한 말이고, 나쁜 습관이나 편견처럼 바뀌기 어려운 상태가 될 때 많이 써요. '고착화되다'라고도 해요.

phrases.en: Bad habits easily become fixed.
phrases.nuance_ko: '고착되다'와 거의 같고, 점점 굳어 가는 과정을 더 느끼게 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Nearly the same, with more feeling of a gradual hardening.

phrases.en: Once formed, a prejudice hardens easily.
phrases.nuance_ko: 더 부드럽고 일상적인 말로, 말할 때 쓰기 좋아요.
phrases.nuance_en: A softer, everyday word that suits speech.

phrases.en: An image that has become fixed is hard to change.
phrases.nuance_ko: 바뀌지 않게 굳은 생각이나 모습을 꾸며 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes an idea or image that has become unchanging.

explain_en: Habits or ideas harden and resist change; formal, often negative. It is similar to '굳어지다' but more formal, and it is often used when something like a bad habit or prejudice settles into a state that is hard to change. You can also say '고착화되다'.

dis.h: becomes stuck or entrenched, hard to change
gh: fastened or set so it won't move

p.n: 고정되다 means set in place; it does not carry the sense of a habit becoming entrenched.

t90.ax: In that region, poverty has become entrenched.

en: to be embodied; to be incarnated

examples.en: The new feature will be implemented next week.
The designer's idea was realized just as it was.

examples.ko: 꿈이 현실로 구현되는 날이 올 거예요.
examples.en: The day will come when the dream becomes reality.
This feature hasn't been implemented yet.
The world in the game was recreated as if it were real.
Please wait until the plan is carried out.

explain: '만들어지다'보다 딱딱하고, 계획이나 아이디어, 기능이 실제로 나타난다는 말이에요. 컴퓨터, 디자인, 정책 이야기에 자주 나와요. 만드는 쪽은 '구현하다'예요.

phrases.en: That feature has not been implemented yet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 계획한 것이 아직 실제로 만들어지지 않았을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when something planned has not been made real yet.

phrases.en: My childhood dream finally came true.
phrases.nuance_ko: '구현되다'와 비슷하지만 꿈이나 희망이 이루어질 때 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 구현되다, but used more for dreams and hopes coming true.

phrases.en: The new service is being implemented little by little.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금 만들어지는 중이라는 진행의 느낌을 줘요.
phrases.nuance_en: Gives a sense that it is in progress right now.
phrases.en_equiv: to be in the process of being realized

explain_en: Stiffer than '만들어지다'; it says a plan, idea or feature has actually appeared. Common in talk about computing, design and policy. The maker's side is '구현하다'.

examples.en: The whole world watched the spacecraft return.
The airport was crowded at the news of the team's return.
I'm worried because the return date hasn't been set.

examples.ko: 오랜 여행 끝에 마침내 귀환이 이루어졌어요.
examples.en: After a long journey, the return finally happened.
I watched a movie called The Hero's Return.
Everyone prayed for the probe's safe return.

explain: 멀리 갔던 사람이나 우주선, 군대가 원래 있던 곳으로 돌아오는 일에 격식 있게 써요. 일상에서 집에 돌아올 때는 '귀가'나 '돌아오다'를 써요. '무사 귀환'이라는 말을 자주 들어요.

phrases.en: The families prayed for the players' safe return.
phrases.nuance_ko: 위험한 곳에 갔다가 다치지 않고 돌아오기를 바랄 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Commonly used when hoping someone returns safely from a risky trip.

phrases.en: Citizens welcomed the team's return.
phrases.nuance_ko: 돌아온 사람들을 맞이할 때 격식 있게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A formal way to say people welcomed those who came back.

phrases.en: The soldiers' return was reported on the news.
phrases.nuance_ko: 돌아온다는 소식을 전할 때 뉴스에서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used in news reports about someone coming back.

explain_en: Formal return from space, war, or abroad. A formal word for a person, spacecraft, or army coming back to where it started after going far away. For coming home in daily life use '귀가' or '돌아오다'. You often hear the phrase '무사 귀환' (safe return).

t90.ax: I watched a movie called The Hero's Return.

examples.ko: 까딱하면 지각할 것 같아서 택시를 탔어요.
examples.en: I might easily be late, so I took a taxi.

examples.ko: 길이 얼어서 까딱하면 넘어질 수 있어요.
examples.en: The road is icy, so you could easily fall with one wrong step.

examples.ko: 이 일은 까딱하면 큰 사고로 이어져요.
examples.en: One slip in this job can lead to a big accident.
With just a little carelessness, I almost lost the important documents.

examples.ko: 요즘 같은 날씨에는 까딱하면 감기에 걸려요.
examples.en: In weather like this, you catch a cold if you're the slightest bit careless.

examples.ko: 까딱하면 약속을 잊을 것 같아서 메모해 놨어요.
examples.en: I might easily forget the appointment, so I made a note of it.

explain: 조금만 잘못하면 나쁜 결과가 생길 수 있을 때 써요. 보통 뒤에 '-ㄹ 뻔했다', '-ㄹ 수 있다', '-ㄹ 것 같다'가 와요. 좋은 결과를 말할 때는 쓰지 않아요.

phrases.en: If you slip up even a little, there'll be big trouble.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-다가는' 때문에 나쁜 결과를 경고하는 느낌이 더 강해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The -다가는 ending gives a stronger warning of a bad result.

phrases.en: If you make even a small mistake, you could get hurt.
phrases.nuance_ko: '잘못하면'이 붙어 실수의 위험을 더 분명히 보여 줘요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 잘못하면 makes the risk of a mistake clearer.
phrases.en_equiv: if you go wrong even slightly

phrases.example: 자칫하면 약속 시간에 늦을 수 있어요.
phrases.en: If we're not careful, we might be late for the appointment.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜻이 비슷하고 글에서도 말에서도 자연스럽게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar in meaning and natural in both writing and speech.

explain_en: Use it when a small mistake could lead to a bad result. It is usually followed by '-ㄹ 뻔했다', '-ㄹ 수 있다' or '-ㄹ 것 같다'. It is not used for good outcomes.

examples.en: The speed of the fall gets faster and faster.
We confirmed the falling of objects through an experiment.
The parachute drop training has started.
I filmed the ball dropping.
They hit the landing point exactly.
They put up a safety net to prevent falling accidents.

explain: 위에서 아래로 떨어지는 것을 과학이나 훈련 이야기에서 말해요. 일상에서는 '떨어지다'를 쓰고, '낙하'는 '낙하산', '자유 낙하', '낙하 사고'처럼 굳은 말에서 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: The soldier jumped down wearing a parachute.
phrases.nuance_ko: 공중에서 떨어질 때 천천히 내려오게 해 주는 도구예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A device that lets you come down slowly when falling through the air.

phrases.en: An object in free fall gets faster and faster.
phrases.nuance_ko: 과학에서 중력만 받아 떨어지는 것을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: In science, falling under gravity alone.

phrases.en: The ball falls slowly.
phrases.nuance_ko: '낙하'를 동사로 쓴 말로, 설명하는 글에서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The verb form of 낙하, used in explanatory writing.

explain_en: Object dropping through the air, used in physics and technical talk. It is the dropping of something from above, used in science and training contexts. In daily speech people say 떨어지다; 낙하 appears in set terms such as 낙하산 (parachute), 자유 낙하, and 낙하 사고.

examples.ko: 관중이 경기장에 난입해서 경기가 잠시 멈췄어요.
examples.en: A spectator burst onto the field, so the game stopped for a moment.
A stranger suddenly barged into the meeting room.

examples.ko: 고양이가 무대에 난입하는 바람에 모두 웃었어요.
examples.en: A cat wandered onto the stage and everyone laughed.
Fans tried to storm the venue but were stopped by security guards.

examples.ko: 방송 중에 아이가 스튜디오에 난입한 영상이 화제예요.
examples.en: A video of a child bursting into the studio during a broadcast is a hot topic.
I locked the door so people couldn't barge in.

explain: 허락 없이 갑자기, 막무가내로 들어올 때 써요. 그냥 '들어오다'와 달리 소란스럽고 예의 없는 느낌이 있어서 뉴스에서 '경기장에 난입하다'처럼 많이 보여요. 비슷한 말로 '쳐들어오다'가 있어요.

phrases.en: The stadium intrusion incident was on the news.
phrases.nuance_ko: 허락 없이 들어온 일을 뉴스에서 말할 때 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing in the news for an incident of entering without permission.

phrases.en: My friends suddenly barged into my room.
phrases.nuance_ko: '난입하다'보다 일상적이고, 장난스럽게도 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: More everyday than 난입하다, and it can be used playfully too.

phrases.en: The security guard stopped the intrusion.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 '난입'과 함께 허락 없이 들어오는 일을 막는다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Uses the noun 난입 to say someone stopped an unauthorized entry.

explain_en: It is used when someone comes in suddenly and unceremoniously without permission. Unlike plain '들어오다', it feels noisy and rude, and appears in news as in '경기장에 난입하다'. A similar word is '쳐들어오다'.

en: to be disclosed; to be revealed; to be found out

examples.en: What I did in secret was found out in the end.
The thief in hiding gets discovered by the police.
If cheating on an exam is discovered, you are in big trouble.
I was worried the secret would come to light.
Only after being found out did he tell the truth.
I tried not to get caught, but it ended up being discovered.

explain: '들키다'는 일상에서 누구에게나 쓰고, '발각되다'는 나쁜 일이나 비밀이 드러났을 때 뉴스나 글에서 더 많이 써요. 친구나 가족에게 걸렸을 때는 '들켰어요'가 자연스러워요.

phrases.en: Luckily, that matter was not discovered.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비밀이나 잘못이 들키지 않았다는 뜻이에요. 부정형으로 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The secret or wrongdoing was not found out. Often used in the negative.

phrases.en: I worried that the secret would be discovered.
phrases.nuance_ko: 들킬 것을 걱정하거나 겁낼 때 '-ㄹ까 봐'와 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with -ㄹ까 봐 to express fear of being found out.

phrases.en: I ran away quickly before I was discovered.
phrases.nuance_ko: 들키기 직전 시점을 말할 때 쓰는 연결 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A connecting phrase for the moment just before being found out.

explain_en: A secret or hiding person is discovered, usually unwelcome for them. '들키다' is the everyday word for getting caught, while '발각되다' is used more in news and writing when something bad or secret comes out. When your friend or family catches you, '들켰어요' sounds more natural.

t90.ax: I was worried the secret would come to light.

en: to be emitted; to be discharged; (a player) to be released from a team

examples.en: Harmful gas is released from the factory.
Heat in the body is released through sweat.
A large amount of energy was released all at once.

examples.ko: 방출된 물질은 바람을 타고 멀리 퍼졌어요.
examples.en: The released substance spread far on the wind.

examples.ko: 구단에서 방출되면 새 팀을 찾아야 해요.
examples.en: If you are let go by the club, you have to find a new team.
I attached a filter so smoke does not escape.

explain: 방출되다는 열·가스·에너지가 밖으로 나오는 결과를 말할 때 써요. 같은 뜻으로 '나오다', '빠져나가다'가 쉬운 말이에요. 선수가 팀에서 나가게 될 때도 '방출되다'라고 해요.

phrases.en: Smoke comes out of the chimney.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상에서 더 쉽게 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easier word for daily speech.

phrases.en: The heat is not released outside.
phrases.nuance_ko: 밖으로 나가지 않는 상황을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when something does not go out.

phrases.example: 그 선수는 이번 시즌에 팀에서 방출됐어요.
phrases.en: That player was released from the team this season.
phrases.nuance_ko: 선수가 팀을 떠나게 되었을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a player is made to leave the team.
phrases.en_equiv: to be released from a team

explain_en: Passive, heat or gas given off; also a player let go. 방출되다 describes heat, gas or energy ending up released outward; the easier everyday words are '나오다' and '빠져나가다'. A player let go by a team is also '방출되다'.

t90.ax: Harmful gas is released from the factory.

examples.ko: 집에 무슨 변고가 생긴 것 같아요.
examples.en: It seems something terrible has happened at home.
I arrived safely without any trouble.

examples.ko: 갑자기 연락이 끊겨서 변고가 있는지 걱정돼요.
examples.en: Contact suddenly stopped, so I'm worried something has happened.

examples.ko: 이 마을에 큰 변고가 일어난 적이 있어요.
examples.en: A major disaster once happened in this village.

examples.ko: 변고를 알리는 전화를 받고 급히 달려갔어요.
examples.en: I got a call about the bad news and rushed over.
The day passed without anything unusual happening.

explain: 갑자기 생긴 나쁜 일을 말하고, '변고 없이'처럼 아무 일 없다는 말로 자주 써요. '사고'보다 무슨 일인지 막연한 느낌이에요. 놀랄 때 '이게 무슨 변고야?'라고도 해요.

phrases.en: I'm doing well without any trouble.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아무 일 없이 무사하다는 뜻으로 안부를 전할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means safe and without incident, used when reporting how you are.

phrases.example: 밤새 연락이 없어서 무슨 변고가 생겼나 걱정했어요.
phrases.en: There was no contact all night, so I worried something had happened.
phrases.nuance_ko: 갑자기 나쁜 일이 일어났다고 걱정할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when worrying that something bad has suddenly happened.

phrases.example: 갑자기 불이 다 꺼졌어요. 이게 무슨 변고예요?
phrases.en: The lights all went out suddenly. What on earth is going on?
phrases.nuance_ko: 예상 못 한 이상한 일에 놀랐을 때 하는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: What you say when surprised by something unexpected and strange.

explain_en: It refers to a sudden bad event and is often used in the negative sense of '변고 없이' (without incident). Compared with '사고' (accident), it feels vaguer about what exactly happened. People also exclaim '이게 무슨 변고야?' when shocked.

t90.ax: I arrived safely without any trouble.
